papers.title: Effects of Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi and Clay Minerals on Soil Nitrogen and Phosphorus Availability and Microbial Community Responses.
papers.abstract: Efficient management of soil nitrogen and phosphorus availability is important for soil fertility and crop productivity, but the field responses of rhizosphere microbial communities to arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) and clay-mineral amendments remain unclear. A wheat-field experiment compared four treatments: an untreated control (A), bentonite (B; 39 kg plot-1), sepiolite (C; 39 kg plot-1), and AMF inoculation (E; 2.25 kg inoculum plot-1; 120 spores g-1). Each treatment comprised six 4 × 7.5 m plots. Soil physicochemical properties were evaluated using all six plots, whereas rhizosphere m
papers.summary: This field experiment tested how bentonite, sepiolite, and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) inoculation affect soil nitrogen and phosphorus availability and rhizosphere microbial communities in a wheat field. The study compares four treatments across replicated plots to assess whether these amendments improve soil fertility and shift microbial community composition. It provides field-scale evidence on the interplay between mineral amendments, AMF, and soil microbial responses.

papers.title: Gut Microbiome Compositional and Functional Signatures Associated with Chemotherapy Response in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: An Exploratory Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The gut microbiome modulates chemotherapy efficacy in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet its relationship with the clinically relevant endpoint of post-chemotherapy surgical eligibility remains poorly characterised. We explored whether baseline gut microbiome composition and metagenomically predicted metabolic function differ between chemotherapy responders and non-responders in PDAC. Methods: In this prospective single-centre exploratory cohort study, faecal samples were collected from 15 patients with non-immediately resectable PDAC at diagnosis, before chemo
papers.summary: In this small exploratory cohort of 15 pancreatic cancer patients, baseline gut microbiome composition and predicted metabolic function were compared between those who responded to chemotherapy (becoming eligible for surgery) and those who did not. The study identifies compositional and functional microbiome signatures associated with chemotherapy response, suggesting the gut microbiome may help predict or modulate treatment outcomes in PDAC.

papers.title: Modeling association networks from metagenome time series - a proof-of-concept from two contrasting estuaries.
papers.abstract: Understanding microbial responses to environmental gradients is important for ecosystem assessment in estuarine environments. Here, we integrated time-series samples and shotgun metagenomics with association network inference, to examine patterns of taxonomic and functional co-variation. We collected and sequenced eDNA from two sediment time series from neighbouring but environmentally contrasting Basque estuaries, and compared the resulting taxonomic and functional association networks, based on Metagenome Assembled Genomes (MAGs) and KEGG Orthologous Groups (KOs), respectively. Networks infe
papers.summary: The authors sequenced environmental DNA from sediment time series in two contrasting Basque estuaries and built association networks from metagenome-assembled genomes and KEGG orthologs to compare taxonomic and functional co-variation patterns. This proof-of-concept shows that integrating time-series shotgun metagenomics with network inference can reveal how microbial communities respond to environmental gradients, and that contrasting estuaries yield distinguishable network structures.

papers.title: Bacterial community profiles of soils from the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve, Philippines.
papers.abstract: The Mount Makiling Forest Reserve harbors diverse microorganisms with potential biotechnological applications, yet bacterial taxonomic profiling across its watersheds remains limited. Amplicon metagenome sequencing targeting the 16S rRNA gene revealed Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota as dominant phyla, with Actinobacteriota, Verrucomicrobiota, Chloroflexi, Myxococcota, Methylomirabilota, Bacteroidota, Nitrospirota, and Planctomycetota present at varying abundances.
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing to profile bacterial communities in soils from the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve in the Philippines. Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota were the dominant phyla, with ten additional phyla present at varying abundances across watersheds. The work provides a baseline taxonomic survey of an understudied tropical forest soil environment.

papers.title: Hospital Drain Microbiomes as Distinct Microbial Signatures Within Urban Wastewater Networks in the Han River Watershed.
papers.abstract: Background: Hospital drainage systems represent an important interface between healthcare facilities and urban wastewater networks and may contribute distinct microbial inputs to downstream aquatic environments. This issue is particularly relevant in Seoul, Republic of Korea, where urban wastewater discharges into receiving waters within the Han River watershed. Methods: In this study, we characterized hospital drain microbiomes to evaluate their microbial and environmental signatures, using residential drains as a non-clinical comparison. Results: Hospital drains exhibited a distinct taxonomi
papers.summary: This study compared the microbiomes of hospital drains with residential drains in Seoul's Han River watershed, finding that hospital drains harbor distinct taxonomic signatures. The results suggest hospital drainage systems introduce unique microbial inputs into urban wastewater networks that could affect downstream aquatic environments.

papers.title: Functional convergence despite taxonomic turnover across coral-associated microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Coral-associated microbiomes are fundamental to holobiont health and resilience, yet their community structures often demonstrate high taxonomic variability across host species. Whether such variability results in functional instability or reflects pervasive metabolic redundancy remains unclear. Here, we investigated microbial taxonomic structure, functional potential, and community assembly mechanisms across 15 coral species using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and shotgun metagenomics. These communities exhibited extreme taxonomic heterogeneity, high beta-diversity, and the absence of a universall
papers.summary: Across 15 coral species, microbial communities showed extreme taxonomic variability but converged on similar functional potential, indicating pervasive metabolic redundancy. This suggests that coral-associated microbiomes maintain functional stability despite high taxonomic turnover, which may support holobiont resilience.

papers.title: Exploratory Shotgun Metagenomic Analysis of the Fecal Microbiome and Antimicrobial-Resistance Potential in Simmental Calves with Different Diarrheal Statuses.
papers.abstract: Calf diarrhea is frequently accompanied by disruption of the gastrointestinal microbiota, but the relationships between clinical status and microbial community composition, gene-content functional potential, and antimicrobial-resistance-associated features remain incompletely characterized. This exploratory study aimed to characterize these features in calves with different diarrheal statuses using shotgun metagenomics. Six approximately 2-month-old Simmental calves from Chahar Right Middle Banner, Inner Mongolia, were included, comprising two healthy calves, two calves with mild diarrhea, and
papers.summary: This exploratory study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the fecal microbiome and antimicrobial-resistance gene potential of six Simmental calves grouped by diarrheal status (healthy, mild diarrhea, and presumably a third group). It characterizes differences in microbial community composition and functional gene content associated with clinical status, though the very small sample size limits generalizability. The work is preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

papers.title: Limited Gut Microbiome Differences Between Relapsing-Remitting and Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: A Shotgun Metagenomic Study.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome may contribute to multiple sclerosis (MS) pathophysiology, but its relationship with disease phenotype and progression remains unclear. To characterize taxonomic and functional gut microbiome differences between relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) and secondary progressive MS (SPMS) and their associations with neurological disability and circulating biomarkers. This cross-sectional study included 89 participants (30 healthy controls, 29 RRMS, and 30 SPMS). Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was used to assess microbial diversity, taxonomic profiles, and predefined short-chain fatty ac
papers.summary: This cross-sectional shotgun metagenomic study compared gut microbiome composition and function among 30 healthy controls, 29 relapsing-remitting MS patients, and 30 secondary progressive MS patients. The authors found only limited taxonomic and functional differences between RRMS and SPMS, suggesting that gut microbiome shifts do not strongly distinguish these disease phenotypes. Associations with disability and circulating biomarkers were modest, indicating the microbiome's role in MS progression may be less pronounced than hypothesized.

papers.title: From Microbiome Associations to Deployable Precision Probiotics in Animals: A Critical Narrative Review and Proposed Causal Evidence Framework for Next-Generation Probiotic Development.
papers.abstract: Next-generation probiotics (NGPs) are promoted as precision tools for animal health, yet the term is often applied to uncommon taxa before causality, safety and target-species efficacy are established. This critical narrative review reframes animal NGPs as a development pathway rather than a taxonomic category. A structured PubMed search was last run on 14 September 2026 with a publication date cutoff of 1 September 2026 and was supplemented by citation tracing and targeted searches of authoritative sources. From the screened literature, 45 representative and conceptually informative sources w
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This critical narrative review argues that "next-generation probiotics" for animals should be defined as a development pathway—progressing from microbiome association through causal evidence, safety, and target-species efficacy—rather than as a label for any uncommon microbial taxon. Drawing on 45 representative sources, the authors propose a causal evidence framework to guide the translation of microbiome associations into deployable precision probiotics.

papers.title: Integrated Metagenomic and Metatranscriptomic Analysis Reveals Microbiome Differences Between Bisexual and Parthenogenetic Populations of Haemaphysalis longicornis.
papers.abstract: The tick Haemaphysalis longicornis is an important vector of human and animal pathogens in East Asia that comprises both bisexual (Bis) and parthenogenetic (Par) populations. While previous studies have documented differences between these reproductive groups in genome ploidy, host transcription, and vector capacity, it remains unclear whether reproductive strategy is accompanied by systematic divergence in the tick-associated microbiome, including microbial community composition, transcriptional activities, and functional outputs. Here, we profiled laboratory-maintained Bis and Par population
papers.summary: This study compared the microbiome of bisexual and parthenogenetic populations of the tick Haemaphysalis longicornis using integrated metagenomic and metatranscriptomic sequencing. The authors found systematic differences in microbial community composition, transcriptional activity, and functional outputs between the two reproductive groups, suggesting that reproductive strategy is accompanied by microbiome divergence. These findings may help explain previously observed differences in vector capacity between bisexual and parthenogenetic tick populations.

papers.title: Multi-omics profiling reveals gut segment-specific and age-associated microbial restructuring linked to host phenotypic maturation in Taihu geese.
papers.abstract: Taihu geese are valued for efficient utilization of fibrous feed resources and for desirable meat quality, yet how gut microbial organization varies across intestinal regions and physiological stages, and how these changes relate to host phenotype, remains unclear. We integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, ITS sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and host phenotyping to characterize intestinal microbial ecology in Taihu geese at 160 days of age (D160; physiological stability stage) and 450 days of age (D450; late-laying stage). Spatial profiling of the D160 group across the duodenum, jejunum, ileum
papers.summary: This study integrates 16S rRNA, ITS, and shotgun metagenomic sequencing with host phenotyping to map how gut microbial communities differ across intestinal segments and between two physiological stages (160 vs. 450 days) in Taihu geese. It identifies segment-specific and age-associated microbial restructuring that correlates with host phenotypic maturation, highlighting how gut ecology shifts with the host's physiological state.

papers.title: Soil Microbiome Signatures Associated with Epidemiological Heterogeneity Across Natural Plague Foci in Inner Mongolia, China.
papers.abstract: Plague persistence relies on complex host-vector-environment interactions, yet the ecological contribution of soil microbiomes to natural foci remains poorly understood. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 143 soil samples across four distinct plague foci in Inner Mongolia, China, to characterize microbiome features associated with contrasting epidemiological states. Taxonomic, functional, and network analyses showed that the three active plague foci exhibited lower microbial diversity, simplified co-occurrence networks, and enrichment of specific taxa, particularly Streptomyces. Co
papers.summary: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 143 soil samples from four plague foci in Inner Mongolia revealed that active plague foci have lower microbial diversity, simplified co-occurrence networks, and enrichment of specific taxa such as Streptomyces compared to inactive foci. The study links soil microbiome composition and functional potential to epidemiological heterogeneity in natural plague foci.

papers.title: Fast and accurate taxonomic domain assignment of short metagenomic reads using BBERT.
papers.abstract: Shotgun metagenomes from complex environments such as soil uncover vast biodiversity. Yet most short reads produced by shotgun sequencing cannot be taxonomically or functionally annotated, as they lack a sufficiently comprehensive reference, obscuring the true structure and function of microbial communities. We introduce BBERT, a nucleotide large language model optimized for short reads. Testing on a large cohort of soil metagenomes, we found that BBERT identifies bacterial sequence syntax without relying on reference databases, enabling accurate assignment of taxonomic domain, coding potentia
papers.summary: BBERT is a nucleotide large language model trained specifically on short sequencing reads that can assign taxonomic domain (e.g., bacterial vs. other) without relying on reference databases. Tested on a large cohort of soil metagenomes, it accurately identifies bacterial sequence syntax and coding potential, addressing the problem that most short shotgun reads cannot be annotated due to incomplete references.

papers.title: Short-Term Simulated NH4+/NO3- Inputs Reorganize Soil Microbial Communities and Modify N-Cycling Functional Potential in Temperate Forests.
papers.abstract: Forest soil nitrogen (N) turnover and nitrous oxide (N2O) release are strongly influenced by atmospheric N deposition. Although the effects of individual inorganic N species on soil biogeochemistry are well documented, the consequences of changing their relative supply for N2O formation and the underlying microbial pathways remain less clear. We therefore examined soil N2O emissions, microbial communities, and N-transformation potential across a gradient of ammonium-to-nitrate (NH4+/NO3-) inputs in a temperate forest soil from Northeast China. Seven treatments covering NH4+/NO3- ratios from 1:
papers.summary: This study tested how different ratios of ammonium to nitrate inputs affect soil microbial communities and nitrogen cycling in a temperate forest soil from Northeast China. The authors measured N2O emissions, microbial community composition, and nitrogen-transformation potential across a gradient of NH4+/NO3- ratios, finding that short-term simulated N inputs reorganize microbial communities and alter the functional potential for nitrogen cycling. The work highlights how the chemical form of nitrogen deposition, not just total amount, shapes soil microbial processes and greenhouse gas production.

papers.title: Next-Generation Sequencing in Practical Wildlife Disease Investigation: Metagenomic Insights into European Bison and Gazelle Mortality and Morbidity Events.
papers.abstract: Wildlife disease investigations require diagnostic methods capable of detecting diverse and previously unrecognized pathogens. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) was applied to samples from three Dorcas gazelles (Gazella dorcas osiris) affected by sudden mortality and four European bison (Bison bonasus) with respiratory disease or necrotic balanoposthitis (NBP). No dominant bacterial species was detected in gazelles. In European bison, respiratory disease was associated with Pasteurella multocida, whereas NBP samples were dominated by Porphyromonas levii and other anaerobes. Dorcas
papers.summary: This study applied metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to investigate wildlife disease events, analyzing samples from three Dorcas gazelles with sudden mortality and four European bison with respiratory disease or necrotic balanoposthitis. No dominant bacterial pathogen was identified in the gazelles, while respiratory disease in bison was associated with Pasteurella multocida and necrotic balanoposthitis samples were dominated by Porphyromonas levii and other anaerobes. The work demonstrates that mNGS can provide useful pathogen leads in practical wildlife disease investigations where conventional diagnostics fall short.

papers.title: Sketching the SRA: experiment-wide similarity search across 4.8 million metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Recent efforts have demonstrated that systematic analysis of the millions of metagenomes in the Sequence Read Archive (SRA) enables groundbreaking biological discoveries. However, SRA-scale comparison of whole metagenomes has remained elusive. Here, we introduce the most comprehensive resource to date for experiment-to-experiment analysis of all SRA metagenomes, comprising FracMinHash sketches (470GB), hypergen sketches (19GB), and an all-pairs Jaccard similarity matrix (90GB), which we release online at https://github.com/RolandFaure/SRA-metagenome-sketches-databases . These resources enable
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors created a comprehensive resource for comparing all 4.8 million metagenomes in the Sequence Read Archive using compact sketch representations (FracMinHash and hypergen sketches) plus an all-pairs Jaccard similarity matrix, all publicly released. This enables experiment-to-experiment similarity search at SRA scale, which was previously infeasible, opening the door to large-scale metagenomic discovery.

papers.title: Maternal transmission and limited virulent phage replication shape early infant gut virome maturation.
papers.abstract: Early life gut microbiome dynamics are increasingly recognized as important determinants of microbiome maturation, yet the ecological dynamics of its associated bacteriophages remain poorly resolved. Here, we performed bulk and virus like particle (VLP)-enriched metagenomic sequencing and fecal metabolomic profiling of longitudinal fecal samples from 32 mother-infant dyads, incorporating an exogenous phage spike in to enable absolute quantification of viral loads. Our results show that early infant gut phageome is defined by a profound lack of virulent phage genome copies while temperate phage
papers.summary: This study used longitudinal metagenomic and metabolomic profiling of 32 mother-infant pairs, with a spiked-in phage for absolute viral load quantification, to track how the infant gut virome matures. It found that early infant guts contain very few virulent phage genomes, with temperate phages dominating, and that maternal transmission shapes the early virome. The work suggests that virulent phage replication is limited in early life, which may help explain the ecological dynamics of microbiome maturation.

papers.title: Comparative Genomics of Ecologically Differentiated Nitrososphaera-Related Ammonia-Oxidizing Archaea.
papers.abstract: Soil acidification strongly influences the ecology of terrestrial ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA). Within this group, the Nitrososphaera-related alpha (NS-α) and delta (NS-δ) lineages exhibit pronounced pH-associated ecological differentiation. In the preceding microcosm experiment, NS-α populations showed greater persistence than NS-δ during ammonium-driven soil acidification, yet the genomic basis underlying this ecological differentiation remains poorly understood. In this study, metagenomic sequencing of one near-neutral baseline microcosm (pH 7.35) and one acidified microcosm (pH 4.73) wa
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing of soil microcosms at near-neutral (pH 7.35) and acidified (pH 4.73) conditions to compare the genomes of two ecologically differentiated ammonia-oxidizing archaeal lineages, NS-α and NS-δ. The work aims to uncover the genomic basis for the previously observed greater persistence of NS-α under ammonium-driven acidification. It provides a comparative genomic framework linking pH-associated ecological differentiation to specific genomic features in soil AOA.

papers.title: Complementary Use of Shotgun Metagenomics and Multiplex PCR for Pathogen Detection on High-Touch Surfaces.
papers.abstract: Shotgun metagenomics is being increasingly promoted as a pathogen-agnostic alternative to targeted PCR for environmental surveillance, yet its practical value on dry, low-biomass, host-dominated surfaces remains uncertain. In a companion study, we reported QIAstat-Dx multiplex PCR screening of 55 pooled high-touch surface samples from Riyadh, identifying 19 positive pools (34.5%). Here, in a retrospective exploratory comparison, we use those previously reported PCR calls as the targeted comparator and ask what unenriched shotgun metagenomic sequencing adds. Ten archived pools, each with at lea
papers.summary: This study compared shotgun metagenomic sequencing with multiplex PCR for detecting pathogens on high-touch surfaces in Riyadh. Using 10 archived PCR-positive pools, the authors found that unenriched metagenomics adds limited pathogen detection value on dry, low-biomass, host-dominated surfaces, suggesting PCR remains the more practical targeted approach while metagenomics offers complementary context.

papers.title: Taxonomic and Functional Profiles of the Gastrointestinal Microbiome Across Digestive Tract Segments in Growing Water Buffaloes.
papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal segments in ruminants differ in physiological environment and substrate availability. This study characterized taxonomic and gene-encoded functional profiles in 54 shotgun metagenomes from 30 growing male water buffaloes assigned to five dietary formulations. The dataset comprised 30 rumen-fluid samples, six per group, and 24 post-slaughter samples from six gastrointestinal sites in five animals. Comparisons among groups A-E yielded p = 0.9816 for final body weight, p = 0.9315 for overall average daily gain, and p = 0.2832 for rumen-fluid pH. Genus-level principal coordinate a
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to profile the taxonomic and functional composition of the gastrointestinal microbiome across multiple digestive tract segments in growing water buffaloes fed five different diets. The authors found that dietary formulations did not significantly affect final body weight, average daily gain, or rumen pH, and they characterized how microbial communities and gene functions vary along the digestive tract. The dataset provides a segment-resolved reference for the buffalo gut microbiome.

papers.title: First Shotgun Metagenomic Characterization of the Gut Microbiome of the Endangered Longhorn Beetle Callipogon relictus (Coleoptera: Cerambycidae).
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome of Callipogon relictus, a rare member of the family Cerambycidae, was characterized for the first time using shotgun metagenomic sequencing. The aim of this study was to compare the taxonomic diversity and structure of the gut microbial communities in larvae and adults. Bacteria dominated the metagenomic profiles, accounting for 92.47% of the taxonomic composition in adults and 85.31% in larvae. Proteobacteria predominated in the bacterial component of both pooled profiles, accounting for 87.88% and 89.43%, respectively. The pooled adult profile had the highest relative abun
papers.summary: This study provides the first shotgun metagenomic characterization of the gut microbiome of the endangered longhorn beetle Callipogon relictus, comparing larval and adult life stages. Bacteria dominated the communities (92.47% in adults, 85.31% in larvae), with Proteobacteria being the most abundant phylum in both. The work establishes a baseline description of gut microbial diversity in this rare species.

papers.title: Metagenomic Bioprospecting of Bioremediation-Related Genes in Amazonian Aquatic Ecosystems.
papers.abstract: Environmental monitoring of contaminated freshwater systems still lacks curated genomic resources tailored to bioremediation-oriented screening. In this study, we developed a curated catalogue of 546 genes from 80 microbial species associated with heavy-metal resistance, hydrocarbon degradation, detoxification and related functions and applied it to river metagenomes from four municipalities in Pará, Brazilian Amazon: Altamira, Bragança, Marabá and Paragominas. Functional annotation was performed using eggNOG-mapper and metagenomic reads were aligned against the curated catalogue with Bowtie2.
papers.summary: The authors built a curated catalogue of 546 bioremediation-related genes from 80 microbial species, covering heavy-metal resistance, hydrocarbon degradation, and detoxification functions. They applied this catalogue to river metagenomes from four municipalities in the Brazilian Amazon, annotating functions with eggNOG-mapper and aligning reads with Bowtie2. This provides a targeted genomic resource for screening contaminated freshwater systems for bioremediation potential.

papers.title: WasteFams: a database of protein families from global wastewater microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance has emerged as a critical tool for global epidemiology, yet the functional diversity of wastewater microbiomes remains poorly characterized at the protein level. Here, we present WasteFams, the first comprehensive database dedicated to the systematic exploration of protein families in wastewater metagenomic and metatranscriptomic studies worldwide. Integrating data from 580 metagenomes, 132 metatranscriptomes, and 1709 reference genomes (504 metagenomes, 129 metatranscriptomes, and 1151 reference genomes after filtering), WasteFams catalogs 3887 non-redundant protein fa
papers.summary: WasteFams is a new database that catalogs protein families found in wastewater microbiomes worldwide, built by integrating 580 metagenomes, 132 metatranscriptomes, and 1,709 reference genomes (filtered to 504, 129, and 1,151 respectively). It provides the first systematic protein-level characterization of wastewater microbiome functional diversity, yielding 3,887 non-redundant protein families. This resource supports wastewater surveillance and functional microbiome research.

papers.title: Cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing for culture-negative anaerobic central nervous system infection involving Prevotella oris: attribution challenges in low-biomass specimens.
papers.abstract: Anaerobic central nervous system (CNS) infections are uncommon but diagnostically difficult because fastidious organisms may be suppressed by empirical antimicrobial therapy and conventional cultures may remain negative. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) can recover microbial nucleic acids in this setting, but low microbial biomass creates a central attribution problem: a detected organism may represent active infection, introduced commensal DNA, laboratory background, or bioinformatic misclassification. This narrative Mini Review uses Prevotella oris as a
papers.summary: This mini review examines the diagnostic challenges of using cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to identify anaerobic CNS infections, using Prevotella oris as a case example. The authors highlight that low microbial biomass in CSF creates a fundamental attribution problem—detected organisms may reflect true infection, introduced commensal DNA, lab contamination, or bioinformatic misclassification—making clinical interpretation difficult.

papers.title: gTranslate: rapid and accurate translation table prediction for prokaryotic genomes.
papers.abstract: Bioinformatic tools often require the prediction of protein-coding genes to make inferences about prokaryotic genomes. Typically, the genetic code used for translating genes to proteins must be specified by the user based on the taxonomic classification of a genome assembly or, for some widely used tools, established using a heuristic rule based on gene coding densities. Manual specification is at best inconvenient, but more challenging is that many bioinformatic tools are applied before taxonomic classifications have been established making specifying the translation table impractical.
papers.summary: gTranslate is a new tool that predicts the correct genetic code (translation table) for prokaryotic genomes directly from sequence data, avoiding the need for prior taxonomic classification or manual specification. It addresses a common bottleneck in gene prediction pipelines where the translation table must be known before analysis. The tool is designed to be rapid and accurate, improving automation of prokaryotic genome annotation.

papers.title: Metagenomic and metabolomic analysis of the early gut microbiota development in Nipponia nippon.
papers.abstract: The crested ibis (Nipponia nippon) is an endangered bird whose early gut microbiota development remains poorly understood. To address this gap, this study integrated metagenomics and metabolomics to investigate the dynamic succession of gut microbiota and metabolism in naturally hatched chicks during early development.
papers.summary: This study integrates metagenomic and metabolomic profiling to characterize how the gut microbiota and its metabolic output change during early development in naturally hatched crested ibis chicks, an endangered bird species. It provides one of the first longitudinal descriptions of microbiota succession and associated metabolite shifts in this species, offering baseline data that could inform conservation and captive-breeding strategies.

papers.title: Metagenomic and culture-dependent characterization of between-field variation in phosphorus-cycling microbial communities and functional potential across tobacco-safflower rotation fields.
papers.abstract: Rhizosphere microorganisms contribute to soil phosphorus (P) transformation and plant P acquisition, but P-cycling microbial communities and functional associations across tobacco-safflower rotation fields remain poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study combines metagenomic sequencing with culture-based methods to characterize phosphorus-cycling microbial communities in the rhizosphere across different tobacco-safflower rotation fields. It identifies between-field variation in community composition and functional potential related to phosphorus transformation, linking taxonomic profiles to P-cycling genes and cultured isolates. The work provides a baseline characterization of P-cycling microbiomes in this rotation system, though the abstract does not report specific mechanistic or agronomic outcomes.

papers.title: Pathway-level analysis suggests a maintenance-oriented transcriptional response of the ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Nitrosospira sp. NT to acidic pH.
papers.abstract: Acidic environments impose energetic constraints on ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), although some acid-tolerant lineages remain capable of ammonia oxidation at low pH. The transcriptional responses of acid-tolerant AOB to low-pH conditions remain poorly resolved. Here, we characterized the pathway-level response of Nitrosospira sp. NT by integrating a reconstructed metagenome-assembled genome with comparative metatranscriptomic data from cultures incubated for 24 h at pH 5.0 or pH 8.0. Transcript abundance was not uniformly reduced among the metabolic pathways examined at pH 5.0. Genes assoc
papers.summary: The study examines how the acid-tolerant ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Nitrosospira sp. NT responds transcriptionally to low pH (5.0 vs. 8.0) over 24 hours, using a reconstructed metagenome-assembled genome combined with comparative metatranscriptomics. Rather than a uniform shutdown of metabolism, the pathway-level analysis suggests a maintenance-oriented transcriptional response under acidic conditions, with transcript abundance not uniformly reduced across metabolic pathways.

papers.title: Bacterial metagenome in plaque, saliva, and tumor samples from individuals with and without OSCC by next-generation sequencing.
papers.abstract: Oral dysbiosis has been associated with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC); however, most microbiome studies rely on 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing, limiting species-level taxonomic resolution.
papers.summary: This study uses next-generation sequencing to characterize the bacterial metagenome in plaque, saliva, and tumor samples from individuals with and without oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), moving beyond 16S rRNA gene sequencing to achieve species-level taxonomic resolution. The work provides a multi-site survey of oral dysbiosis associated with OSCC, potentially identifying bacterial taxa and functional profiles linked to the disease.

papers.title: Baseline co-occurrence of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Ruminococcus bromii is associated with greater increases in selected short-chain fatty acid-related pathways following resistant starch type 2 intervention across diverse populations.
papers.abstract: Type 2 resistant starch (RS2) can be fermented by the gut microbiota and contribute to short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production; however, microbial responses to resistant starch vary substantially across individuals and populations, and the role of baseline microbiota in this variability remains incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated four publicly available paired metagenomic datasets representing diverse experimental and host contexts and performed cross-dataset analyses of taxonomic and functional responses. Faecalibacterium prausnitzii was among the taxa consistently enriched
papers.summary: By integrating four public paired metagenomic datasets, the authors show that individuals whose baseline gut microbiota already contains both Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Ruminococcus bromii respond to type 2 resistant starch with larger increases in short-chain fatty acid-related pathways. This baseline co-occurrence pattern holds across diverse populations and experimental contexts, suggesting it could serve as a predictor of RS2 responsiveness.
